stories.title: Tishman Speyer, American Express Partner to Offer ZO Access to Non-Tenants
stories.excerpt: Tishman Speyer is partnering with American Express to offer benefits to U.S. Business Platinum Card and the Corporate Platinum Card holders. Reportedly it’s the first such partnership between a major commercial real estate landlord and a credit card issuer. Through the partnership, eligible Amex cardholders will gain access to Tishman Speyer’s ZO amenity network, the first time access has been granted to non-tenants. Eligible Amex Card Members will have access to more than 20 ZO Clubhouse and Studio coworking locations in six major cities: New York, Boston, Washington, DC, Chicago, San Francisco and Los Angeles. The hospitality-driven locations offer venues ranging lounges and coworking areas to meeting and event spaces, with complimentary access, guest passes and up to $500 in annual statement credits toward event space bookings at ZO or Studio locations. For cardholders, there is no increase in the annual fee. The post Tishman Speyer, American Express Partner to Offer ZO Access to Non-Tenants appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Tishman Speyer partners AmEx to open ZO coworking to non-tenants in 6 major metros
First landlord-credit card issuer partnership grants access to 20+ locations across NY, Boston, DC, Chicago, SF, LA
Cardholders get free clubhouse/studio access plus $500 annual event space credits
stories.summary: Tishman Speyer and American Express have launched a first-of-its-kind partnership extending access to Tishman Speyer's ZO coworking and clubhouse network to Business and Corporate Platinum cardholders across six major U.S. markets: New York, Boston, Washington DC, Chicago, San Francisco, and Los Angeles. The partnership opens more than 20 ZO Clubhouse and Studio locations to non-tenants for the first time, offering complimentary access, guest passes, and up to $500 in annual statement credits. There is no additional annual fee for eligible cardholders.
stories.impact: This monetizes Tishman Speyer's real estate footprint and signals confidence in office asset value recovery by driving recurring, high-margin traffic to their buildings. For multifamily developers, this reflects how trophy office landlords are diversifying revenue to offset weakness—relevant as office softness can depress transit-adjacent residential demand in tech-heavy markets like SF and Boston.

stories.title: Skechers Headquarters in Manhattan Beach Listed for Sale
stories.excerpt: CBRE has been named the listing agent for 228 Manhattan Beach Blvd., a nearly 30,000-square-foot office property in Manhattan Beach. The three-story Class A building is being offered through a competitive bidding process and will be delivered vacant. Vice chairmen Stephen Somer and Anthony DeLorenzo and SVPs Bob Healey, John Lane and Brooke Silver are marketing the property on behalf of the ownership, Skechers. The property was extensively renovated in 2018 and serves as a purpose-built corporate headquarters. In addition to office space, the building features a 69-stall private, three-level subterranean parking garage. 228 Manhattan Beach Blvd. also provides an opportunity for retail on the ground floor. “Opportunities to acquire a vacant Class A office building of this scale in downtown Manhattan Beach are exceptionally rare,” said Somer. “The property offers immediate occupancy in one of Southern California’s most established and highly sought-after coastal business communities.” The post Skechers Headquarters in Manhattan Beach Listed for Sale appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Skechers lists 30,000 SF Manhattan Beach HQ for sale, vacant delivery via CBRE competitive bid
Class A 3-story property renovated 2018, includes 69-stall subterranean parking and ground-floor retail
Purpose-built corporate HQ available in rare Manhattan Beach coastal location
stories.summary: Skechers is marketing its Manhattan Beach corporate headquarters—a 30,000-square-foot Class A office property at 228 Manhattan Beach Blvd.—through a competitive bidding process managed by CBRE. The three-story building was extensively renovated in 2018 and features a 69-stall private subterranean parking garage plus ground-floor retail opportunity. Delivery is vacant.
stories.impact: Skechers' HQ sale signals footwear/apparel companies may be consolidating or relocating away from coastal Southern California hubs, reducing local corporate headcount and weakening nearshore residential demand in Manhattan Beach and neighboring beach communities. Any buyer transformation (e.g., to flex office or mixed-use) could reshape local employment.

stories.title: Tech Employment Training Group Signs Headquarters Lease in Long Island City
stories.excerpt: Newmark arranged an approximately 41,000-square-foot lease for Pursuit Transformation Company Inc. at The JACX, a new 700,000-square-foot Class A office development at 28-07 Jackson Ave. in Long Island City. Newmark President, New York Tri-State Region David Falk and Executive Managing Director Daniel Levine represented Pursuit in the lease negotiations. Building owner Tishman Speyer was represented in-house by Megan Sheehan. Pursuit, a nonprofit social impact organization focused on providing employment training and professional development for careers in technology and AI, signed a long-term lease for the entire 14th and 15th floors, where the organization will relocate its New York headquarters.  “The JACX provides Pursuit with an exceptional environment to support its continued growth and evolution,” said Levine. “The new headquarters will allow the organization to build on its strong presence in Long Island City while creating a workplace that supports its people, mission and long-term objectives.”  The post Tech Employment Training Group Signs Headquarters Lease in Long Island City appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Pursuit Transformation Company (nonprofit tech training) signs 41,000 SF lease in Long Island City
Tishman Speyer's JACX (700,000 SF Class A) lease drives HQ relocation to floors 14-15
Tech/AI employment training org signals growth in LIC, strengthening local job and rental demand
stories.summary: Pursuit Transformation Company Inc., a nonprofit focused on employment training and professional development in technology and AI, has signed a long-term lease for approximately 41,000 square feet on floors 14 and 15 of The JACX, a new 700,000-square-foot Class A office development at 28-07 Jackson Ave. in Long Island City. Pursuit is relocating its New York headquarters to the property.
stories.impact: Pursuit's HQ move to Long Island City confirms tech-adjacent employment training is clustering in the submarket, signaling sustained job-creation demand and white-collar population attraction to LIC. This bolsters multifamily fundamentals in Queens waterfront submarkets, supporting rent growth and new residential development pipeline absorption in an already high-velocity rental market.

stories.title: Lewis Group Opens Second NorCal Rental-Home Community in West Sacramento
stories.excerpt: Independence in West Sacramento, a new gated community of 208 townhome-style rental homes developed by Lewis Apartments, opened its leasing office and model homes to the public on Saturday, Oct. 24. Located in West Sacramento’s Southport/Bridgeway Island area, Independence introduces rental homes designed for residents who want the space and privacy of a single-family home without the responsibilities and costs of homeownership. Independence in West Sacramento is Lewis’ second Independence rental-home community in Northern California, following Independence in Dixon in 2025. Building on the momentum of the Dixon and West Sacramento communities, Lewis plans to expand the Independence concept to additional Northern California markets, with future communities planned in Folsom, Vacaville, Fairfield, Newark and other locations. “The success of Independence in Dixon showed us there is strong demand for rental homes that offer more space, privacy and the features people value in a home, without giving up the flexibility and convenience of renting,” said Randall Lewis of Lewis Group of Companies. The post Lewis Group Opens Second NorCal Rental-Home Community in West Sacramento appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Lewis Apartments opens Independence in West Sacramento: 208 rental townhomes, second NorCal location
Follows Dixon 2025 opening; planned expansion to Folsom, Vacaville, Fairfield, Newark and others
Single-family rental (SFR) model shows strong demand for space/privacy vs. traditional apt living
stories.summary: Lewis Apartments has opened Independence in West Sacramento, a gated community of 208 townhome-style rental homes in the Southport/Bridgeway Island area. This is Lewis's second Independence SFR community in Northern California, following Independence in Dixon (opening 2025). Lewis plans to expand the concept to additional markets including Folsom, Vacaville, Fairfield, and Newark, capitalizing on demonstrated demand for rental homes offering space and privacy without homeownership responsibilities.
stories.impact: Lewis's rapid SFR rollout across Northern California suburbs (West Sacramento, Dixon, Folsom, Vacaville, Fairfield, Newark) signals a structural shift in renter preferences toward single-family homes and away from traditional multifamily, particularly in lower-cost inland markets. This represents direct competition to traditional garden apartments and signals supply diversification risk; multifamily developers should monitor local market-specific absorption and rent trends in these expanding SFR markets to adjust product mix and underwriting assumptions.

stories.title: Owner-Occupant Pays $25M for East Rutherford Industrial
stories.excerpt: Lee & Associates New Jersey Office arranged the $25-million sale of 180 Manor Rd., an 86,000-square-foot warehouse property in East Rutherford. The firm’s Troy Wisse, Michael Schaible and Eduardo Lopez represented seller Terreno Realty Corporation and procured the buyer. The purchase of 180 Manor Rd. represents an expansion move for the buyer and will serve as the company’s new headquarters. The location and quality of the building were major considerations. “The buyer already operates from a nearby building, so this acquisition allows the company to remain in the area while gaining a high-quality facility that can accommodate future growth,” said Wisse. “For industrial owner-users today, finding quality properties available for purchase can be challenging, particularly in high-barrier-to-entry markets. Our team’s market expertise enabled us to identify a buyer whose needs aligned with the property and successfully close the transaction.” The property provides convenient access to routes 17 and 3, I-80, I-280 and the New Jersey Turnpike at Exit 16W. The post Owner-Occupant Pays $25M for East Rutherford Industrial appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Owner-occupant purchases 86,000 SF East Rutherford warehouse for $25M via Lee & Associates
Buyer expands from nearby location; building serves as new HQ with future growth capacity
Industrial owner-user demand remains strong; quality inventory in high-barrier markets scarce
stories.summary: Lee & Associates New Jersey arranged the $25 million sale of 180 Manor Rd., an 86,000-square-foot warehouse property in East Rutherford. An owner-occupant buyer, already operating from a nearby building, purchased the property to relocate and expand its headquarters. The location provides convenient access to routes 17 and 3, I-80, I-280, and the New Jersey Turnpike at Exit 16W.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily; however, owner-user industrial consolidation in North Jersey reflects stable regional logistics/light manufacturing employment, which underpins stable renter base for multifamily in adjacent Essex and Hudson County submarkets. Rising industrial property scarcity may push owner-users to seek opportunities in adjacent submarkets, reshaping employment distribution.

stories.title: CP Group Sells Third Boca Raton Office for $79M
stories.excerpt: CP Group has sold off yet another office complex in Boca Raton, Fla. The office investor, alongside Chicago-based Harrison Street Asset Management, sold One Boca Place for $78.9 million, property records show. Golden East Investors purchased the 286,890-square-foot asset at 2255 Glades Road, located just west of Interstate 95, near the Town Center at Boca Raton indoor mall. The two-building office property was constructed in 1986 on a 7.6-acre parcel. City National Bank of Florida provided an $82.1 million loan to the New York-based buyer. The sale produced little appreciation for the sellers, who bought the complex for $76.4 million in 2014. The transaction marks the third office property since the summer that CP Group has sold in Boca Raton, where it is headquartered. In September, the firm sold the Two Town Center property for $62 million to Joe Sitt’s Thor Equities. This summer, it also offloaded the 124-acre, 1.7-million-square-foot BRiC campus for an undisclosed amount to Stephen Ross’s Related Ross. Representatives for CP Group and Golden East Investors did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserserv.com.
bullets: CP Group and Harrison Street sell One Boca Place for $78.9M; minimal 10-year appreciation from $76.4M 2014 buy
286,890 SF two-building office complex (1986, 7.6 acres); third Boca Raton office exit since summer
Buyer Golden East Investors financed via City National Bank $82.1M loan; trophy office softness evident
stories.summary: CP Group and Harrison Street Asset Management sold One Boca Place in Boca Raton, Florida, for $78.9 million to Golden East Investors. The 286,890-square-foot two-building office property at 2255 Glades Road (built 1986 on 7.6 acres) yielded minimal appreciation from CP's $76.4 million purchase in 2014. City National Bank of Florida provided an $82.1 million loan to the buyer. This marks CP Group's third Boca Raton office disposition since summer, following sales of Two Town Center and the BRiC campus.
stories.impact: CP Group's office liquidation strategy in Boca Raton signals loss of confidence in South Florida office fundamentals despite strong population immigration. Flat 10-year returns indicate office cap-rate compression and structural demand uncertainty; multifamily developers should view Boca's office softness as a headwind to ancillary mixed-use retail and co-tenancy value, and a sign that downstream office-worker population in-migration may be weaker than demographic trends suggest.

stories.title: New York City’s Pied-à-Terre Surcharge Changes the Investment Calculation
stories.excerpt: Whether you’re selling a walk-up with a restaurant downstairs, a rental building or a luxury apartment, new rules can change what a property is worth and who will buy it. That’s why New York City’s pied-à-terre surcharge belongs in the investment conversation. The tax doesn’t apply to all these properties, but the differences in how they are treated matter when buyers compare their options. The measure was heralded as a levy on absentee billionaires, projected to bring in around $500 million in new annual revenue for the city. Mayor Zohran Mamdani called it a tax when he announced its rollout over the summer. The law calls it a surcharge. Trystan Polsinelli. PHOTO: Courtesy Compass The legal distinction matters. Ongoing lawsuits challenge whether its revenue can be excluded from the city’s constitutional real estate tax limit. Separate litigation has challenged how the city identified properties potentially subject to the charge. The courts will decide those issues. In the meantime, buyers and sellers have deals to negotiate. Who owned the property, who lived there, and whether it was held through a trust or an LLC are all questions that can affect whether the charge applies, what the property costs to own, and what a buyer is willing to pay. Whatever the name, the surcharge is an additional annual expense for properties where it applies. For the 2026–27 and 2027–28 tax years, affected residential condos and co-ops face rates of 4 percent to 6.5 percent of the applicable Department of Finance value. That’s the city’s valuation, not necessarily the purchase price. Some second-home owners also stand to lose a co-op or condo tax abatement they’ll no longer qualify for. Co-op owners face a particular concern. A charge associated with one apartment is billed through the co-op corporation, rather than billed directly to that unit’s shareholder. bullets: NYC pied-à-terre surcharge (legally a tax despite label) challenges residential investment returns; $500M projected annual revenue
Ongoing litigation targets revenue exclusion from constitutional tax cap and property identification methodology
Affects owner-occupancy, trust/LLC structures; complicates buyer/seller negotiations on multifamily and condo sales
stories.summary: New York City's pied-à-terre surcharge—characterized as a levy on absentee owners, projected to generate approximately $500 million in annual revenue—is reshaping residential investment calculations across multifamily, condo, and rental building sales. The measure is subject to ongoing litigation challenging both its revenue treatment under the city's constitutional real estate tax cap and the city's property identification methodology. Questions around prior ownership, occupancy, and entity structure (trust, LLC) now materially affect deal pricing and buyer qualification.
stories.impact: The pied-à-terre surcharge introduces uncertainty and cost into Manhattan multifamily valuations and exit assumptions, particularly for buildings with transient or absentee investor ownership. Multifamily developers should lower cap-rate assumptions and adjust hold periods for high-end Manhattan rental developments until litigation resolves; buyer pool narrowing (excluding foreign and pass-through investors) weakens demand and complicates refinancing/disposition underwriting.

stories.title: Revamp NYC Wants to Bring 99 Units to the Financial District’s 160 Pearl Street
stories.excerpt: Manhattan’s Financial District was once known only for offices and workers, with its liveliness ending at the close of happy hour. But over the last several years, the neighborhood has transformed into a hub of residential communities. The latest residential project getting added to the mix might be a 99-unit rental. Revamp NYC, a New York-based residential development and property construction firm, has filed an application with the New York City Department of Buildings (DOB) for a new housing development at 160 Pearl Street. If approved, the proposed mixed-use building would stand 25 stories and include 99 units, as well as amenities such as indoor and outdoor recreation space, a yoga room, and 2,394 square feet of ground-floor retail space. Revamp’s Israel Tishler submitted the plans and is listed as the property owner on the DOB application, while Navkiran Cheema of KMA Designs is named as the architect and applicant. Revamp and KMA Designs did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s requests for comment. It is unclear if Revamp intends to make 160 Pearl Street an affordable housing property. Under New York’s 485-x tax incentive, buildings with 99 or fewer units can get a significant tax break when building affordable housing, while not being subject to certain construction worker wage requirements that are mandatory in larger projects of 100 units or more. It’s also unclear whether Revamp plans to demolish the existing six-story commercial building at 160 Pearl Street, which is home to financial consultancy firms Ikahn Capital and Hybrid Funder, as well as Irish pub The Full Shilling in the ground-floor retail space. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Revamp NYC files DOB application for 99-unit, 25-story mixed-use at 160 Pearl Street, Financial District
Project includes 2,394 SF ground-floor retail, indoor/outdoor recreation, yoga room
Affordable housing intent unclear; Financial District residential transformation accelerating
stories.summary: Revamp NYC has filed a Department of Buildings application for a new mixed-use residential development at 160 Pearl Street in Manhattan's Financial District. The proposed 25-story building would include 99 rental units, ground-floor retail (2,394 square feet), and amenities including indoor/outdoor recreation space and a yoga room. The affordability status of the project remains unclear.
stories.impact: Revamp's pipeline addition to the Financial District reflects accelerating residential conversion from post-pandemic office doldrums, signaling strong institutional confidence in FiDi rental demand recovery. For multifamily developers, this indicates a narrowing window to acquire conversion-ready office sites in the submarket before land values reset; existing residential projects in the FiDi (Brooklyn Bridge Park, lower Fulton) should expect intensified supply competition and potential rent moderation as new pipeline absorbs.

stories.title: Rexford Sells $1.3B in SoCal Industrial Assets as Leasing Rebounds
stories.excerpt: Rexford Industrial Realty continued its transformation from Southern California’s biggest industrial buyer into one of its largest sellers during the third quarter after completing $1.3 billion in property sales. The Los Angeles-based real estate investment trust (REIT) sold 25 properties totaling 5.5 million square feet during the quarter, including the previously announced $1.2 billion sale to EQT Real Estate. Rexford has now sold $1.5 billion in properties this year as part of its $2 billion portfolio realignment strategy. CEO Laura Clark said during the REIT’s third-quarter earnings call Friday that the company expects to complete most of the remaining $500 million in planned sales by the end of this year, although rising Treasury yields could complicate deals. “While recent increases in Treasury rates are impacting the cost of capital for certain buyers, and bringing more selectivity to the transaction market, engagement around the remaining disposition assets remains constructive,” Clark said. The EQT portfolio sale, Rexford’s largest deal ever, had a weighted average remaining lease term of just 2.7 years with rents nearly 30 percent above market rates, according to Chief Operating Officer John Nahas. The company also sold three properties totaling approximately 251,000 square feet to owner-users for $86 million. Conversely, Rexford made no acquisitions during the third quarter. Clark said acquisitions remain part of Rexford’s long-term strategy, but not at the expense of other investments. “Today, other uses of capital are more compelling,” she said. “We can afford to be patient. … Our portfolio realignment objective was about owning the right real estate and the right markets.” Meanwhile, Rexford recorded 116 leases covering 3.74 million square feet during the third quarter, up from 2.1 million square feet the previous quarter, and up from the 3.27 million square feet in the same quarter last year. bullets: Rexford Industrial completes $1.3B in SoCal industrial sales (25 properties, 5.5M SF) in Q3
Portfolio realignment strategy targets $2B total divestitures; $500M remaining by year-end
Rising Treasury yields slow deal velocity; leasing momentum remains constructive
stories.summary: Rexford Industrial Realty completed $1.3 billion in Southern California industrial property sales during Q3, selling 25 properties totaling 5.5 million square feet, including a $1.2 billion portfolio sale to EQT Real Estate. The REIT has now divested $1.5 billion of its planned $2 billion portfolio realignment program, with CEO Laura Clark expecting to complete most of the remaining $500 million by year-end. However, rising Treasury yields are creating headwinds for transaction completion, though engagement around remaining assets remains constructive.
stories.impact: Rexford's pivot from buyer to seller of trophy SoCal industrial reflects capital gains realization and anticipated cap-rate expansion; rising Treasury yields signal potential headwinds to multifamily valuations and financing availability regionally. The supply of $500M+ of industrial dispositions still in pipeline (Q4 2024 timeframe) could pressure industrial cap rates and redirect capital away from other CRE segments including multifamily, complicating financing and acquisition strategies in Southern California through late 2024 and into 2025.

stories.title: Roof of Concept: Meet Jeff Thramann, a Data Center Disruptor
stories.excerpt: Jeff Thramann has always been an outside-the-box thinker. A trained neurosurgeon with a degree from Cornell Medical School, Thramann is an entrepreneur at heart and an inventor by nature. He’s been issued north of 130 patents and has seen his inventive startups like U.S. Radiosurgery sold to a publicly traded company and Denver CyberKnife (another cancer treatment facility) bought by a private firm. But it was in the renewable energy space — particularly his interest in creating technology that mitigates the effects of air pollution — where Thramann found his current calling, one that has indirectly pushed him into the data center space, where he and a well-known former politician are creating a new innovation that may disrupt the entire data center industry. Today, Thramann is the CEO of LT350, a data center infrastructure company he formed last year with former U.S. Secretary of Defense Mark Esper, which aims to install mini data centers on the roofs of solar power canopies above the open-air parking lots of properties such as malls, hospitals or schools. The thinking is this: By integrating solar panels with small modular cartridges that consist of graphics processing units (GPU), battery storage and inverters, the tech-fitted roof will essentially turn the airspace above any parking lot into a data center for low latency inference. How Thramann got to this new business plan is a story in itself. After investing into solar panels and the uses of battery-powered technology 20 years ago, Thramann was drawn to electric cars through an association made with Kimle Musk (Elon’s brother) in Boulder, Colo. (Fun fact: Thramann purchased Tesla car No. 541 off the assembly line back in 2008.) bullets: LT350 (CEO Thramann, backed by former SecDef Esper) launches rooftop mini data center canopy model
Solar-integrated modular data center cartridges deployed on malls, hospitals, schools, parking lots
Disruptive tech could reshape data center siting, energy economics, and adjacent real estate demand
stories.summary: LT350, founded by inventor Jeff Thramann and former U.S. Secretary of Defense Mark Esper, is developing a novel data center infrastructure concept: mini modular data centers integrated into solar power canopies above open-air parking lots at properties such as malls, hospitals, and schools. The approach aims to mitigate air pollution while creating localized compute capacity.
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to multifamily development; however, if LT350's distributed rooftop data center model gains traction, it could disintermediate large hyperscale data center development and reduce the anchor tenant draw for tech-centric multifamily clustering around traditional data center hubs (e.g., Northern Virginia, Phoenix). This represents a longer-term structural risk to multifamily demand assumptions in data-center-dependent markets; developers should monitor adoption of edge computing and distributed models when underwriting tech-driven metros.
